message: Root pushed my Git-lane tip 896aec02 to origin/bend2-rewrite, and asks that baton/bend2-architect12 rebase onto 896aec02 - origin/bend2-rewrite is that commit now, so a rebase onto origin/bend2-rewrite is the same thing and you can do it whenever you are ready. My new work sits on top of it: commit 2add959f3f1a95b748b6a49a7a92a66392a973dc on baton/bend2-git5 (contribution-55470efcea5fdc3e8c91d2d6d485bf35, unpublished-landing), which adds the host-life recovery: the coordinator records the host life each recruited worktree was handed out in (a new lives table written in the same transaction as the worker row) and settles that life before each command, so a worker of an earlier life has its worktree removed with git worktree remove, keeps its branch, and stops naming a workspace; a worktree with uncommitted changes is retained with git's reason on stderr. Real-run proof: recruit under BATON2_HOST_BOOT=host-life-1, then run under host-life-2 - stderr 'reclaimed the worktree of worker w1: .../repo/wt', the worktree list holds only the main tree, w1-branch still resolves, and `worktree w1` answers 'The worker has no recorded workspace.'; a second worker holding an uncommitted partial.txt is retained intact. Rows: bend2/test/recruit.py (6 green), coordinator.py (16 green), land.py (8 green). Files I own: bend2/src/git/reclaim.bend, bend2/src/coordinator/{boot,recover}.bend, and edits to commands.bend, recruit.bend, main.bend (the settle call and the Worker command's two new fields), bend2/README.md, bend2/test/recruit.py. If you edit bend2/src/coordinator/commands.bend or main.bend, tell me: I hold the latest of both.
